headline: STI rose 0.6% to 4,962.64 on Thursday, shaking off the US tariff plan; banks and REITs rebounded, Seatrium fell a fifth day. Asia and Europe bounced as AI stocks recovered while the US was shut for Thanksgiving; US trades a half day Friday. Brent near US$91; a Dec Fed hike stays live.

sectors.why: No sector-specific news; the broad market rebounded on Thursday but one day does not set a direction.
No new telco news. Singtel goes ex-dividend (S$0.09) on 30 Nov, which usually lowers the price by about the dividend on that day.
No sector-specific news; the proposed US Section 301 tariff of up to 20% is a later risk for goods exporters, with nothing before early 2027.
No sector-specific news; local inflation stays low, which keeps cost pressure mild.
No sector-specific news.
No sector-specific news; US tariff plans are a mild risk for trade-linked distributors next year.

Chip stocks bounced in Asia on Thursday after the AI sell-off, but Nvidia fell another 3.9% on Wednesday and electronics are about 45% of Singapore's US exports exposed to the tariff plan. Too mixed to call.
Brent rose 0.5% to about US$91 on Strait of Hormuz shipping tension, but oil has swung widely; no clear month-long direction.
DBS, OCBC and UOB rose 0.6-0.9% and REITs led the STI (MPACT, MIT +1.8%) on Thursday. A US Fed hike in December is still seen as live after hot PCE inflation, which caps REITs.

No sector-specific news; healthcare and medical devices are about 15% of goods exposed to the proposed US tariff, but nothing applies before early 2027.
Seatrium fell for a fifth day (-3.7% to S$1.31) after cutting yards from 15 to 11 and about 220 jobs; Morgan Stanley's target is S$1.16. Other engineers such as Keppel and ST Engineering rose.

Petrochemicals are about 28% of Singapore goods exposed to the proposed US tariff of up to 20% (10% with a deal); comments close 5 Jan, so this is a slow-moving risk.

The US Section 301 plan of up to 20% on Singapore goods is a headwind for equipment and component exporters, though analysts note it largely restores earlier tariff levels and starts no earlier than 2027.

No Singapore-specific news; global AI stocks rebounded Thursday in Asia and Europe after two days of heavy selling, but the mood is fragile.
Singapore Airlines fell 1.7% and SATS 0.6% on Thursday with no clear news; high oil (Brent about US$91) is a cost headwind.
No new sector news; Sembcorp Industries was flat on Thursday.
